title: Session Prefetch Orchestrator — Design Spec
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This document describes the design for the Session Prefetch Orchestrator (SPO), a runtime component that proactively prefetches model KV/prefixes and warms model variants to reduce tail latency for conversational sessions while keeping per-tenant cost within SLO-bound budgets. The spec covers architecture, telemetry contract, API surface, runtime decision flow, rollout plan, and operational controls.

Context and motivation

- Problem: conversational workloads on Redwood's hosted and dedicated surfaces exhibit occasional latency spikes caused by cold KV cache misses, model variant cold starts, and cross-tenant eviction contention. These spikes increase user-facing latency and token-cost variance.
- Objective: improve p95/p99 latency consistency for conversational sessions (particularly short interactive sessions) without materially increasing token-costs (>5% uplift target) for typical tenants.

Goals

- Primary: reduce p95 generation latency for interactive conversational routes by 20-35% for sessions with repeat-turns within a 60s window.
- Secondary: keep increased total token-equivalent cost per-session to <5% for 95% of tenants; provide per-tenant cost guardrails and opt-out.
- Observable: provide telemetry to attribute prefetch activity to latency improvements and cost deltas.

Non-goals

- This spec does not change per-token pricing or billing logic; cost accounting is advisory for rollout.
- This is not a replacement for global KV cache design; it is a session-scoped coordination layer.

High-level architecture

Components:
- Prefetch Coordinator (service): central decision-maker for whether to prefetch for an active session. Deployed as a replicated stateless service colocated with serving infra in each region.
- Workload Profiler (library + offline jobs): produces profiles that predict session turn intervals, average sequence lengths, and candidate prefixes, using sampling of historical telemetry.
- Prefetch Predictor (microservice): lightweight ML model (logistic/decision tree ensemble) that scores probability of next turn within thresholds.
- Local Prefetch Cache (runtime store): per-node store holding prefetched KV/prefixes and warmed model variant instances (warm slots) with TTL and eviction metadata.
- Admission Controller (policy engine): enforces per-tenant budgets and global throttle policies.
- Telemetry/Observability (instrumentation contract): a detailed metrics/logs/traces schema so product and SRE teams can measure effectiveness.

Data flow (overview)

1. Session begins and the serving runtime attaches an SPO session id.
2. Serving runtime emits session-start event to the Prefetch Coordinator with last-turn metadata.
3. Prefetch Coordinator queries the Prefetch Predictor and Workload Profiler to decide prefetch intent and a list of prefixes/variants.
4. Admission Controller checks budget/quota and either approves or rejects.
5. Approved prefetch tasks are dispatched to Local Prefetch Cache for async warming; progress and completion are emitted as telemetry.
6. Serving runtime consumes warmed prefixes/kvs and selects warmed variant when available; fallback to usual path if warm not available.

APIs and contracts

- POST /v1/prefetch/decide
  - Payload (JSON):
    {
      "session_id": "string",
      "tenant_id": "string",
      "route": "string",
      "last_turn_seq_len": 128,
      "last_turn_time": "2029-03-15T12:01:12Z",
      "turn_count": 3
    }
  - Response (JSON):
    {
      "should_prefetch": true,
      "candidates": ["prefix_hash_1","prefix_hash_2"],
      "variants": ["gptx-8q", "gptx-16b-faster"],
      "priority": "low|medium|high",
      "expires_in_ms": 45000
    }

Telemetry contract (required metrics)

- Instruments must be emitted with session_id, tenant_id, route, region tags.
- Key metrics (per-minute aggregates and histograms):
  | metric_name | type | description | unit | SLO/target |
  |---|---|---|---:|---|
  | prefetch.attempts | counter | number of prefetch decisions made | count | - |
  | prefetch.approved | counter | prefetch tasks admitted by Admission Controller | count | - |
  | prefetch.completed | counter | prefetch tasks that finished warming | count | - |
  | prefetch.latency| histogram | time from decision to completion | ms | p95 < 2000ms |
  | prefetch.hit | counter | serving observed and used a prefetched prefix/kv | count | - |
  | session.p95_gen_latency_with_prefetch | gauge | p95 generation latency for sessions where prefetch hit | ms | target 20% reduction vs baseline |
  | session.p95_gen_latency_without_prefetch | gauge | comparator baseline | ms | - |
  | cost.delta.token_equiv | histogram | estimated token-equivalent cost delta attributed to prefetch | tokens | p95 < 5% |
  | admission.dropped_by_budget | counter | prefetch rejected due to budget | count | - |

- Traces: each prefetch request must be trace-linked to session start and model-invoke spans. Logs for rejection must include reason codes: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, GLOBAL_THROTTLE, PREDICTOR_LOW_CONFIDENCE.

Decision logic and heuristics

- Decision inputs: predictor score, last-turn interval, tenant SLA tier, per-route historic reuse frequency, model variant warm cost (tokens to warm), and current cluster congestion.
- Thresholds (examples):
  - Only prefetch when predictor_prob > 0.55 and expected_reuse_score > 0.3.
  - For free-tier tenants: require predictor_prob > 0.75 (guarded default).
  - If expected warm token cost > 200 tokens and predicted hit probability < 0.9, skip prefetch.

Prefetch types

- Light-prefetch: prefetch short prefixes (first N key blocks) — low cost, used for low-confidence predictions.
- Variant-warm: start a warmed variant instance (reserve warm slot) — higher cost, used for high-confidence predictions for premium tenants.
- Composite: do both, with staged fallback.

Eviction and TTL

- Per-node Local Prefetch Cache entries have TTL default 60s with soft-eviction based on LRU augmented by priority.
- Warm slots: tracked as ephemeral warm instances with gradual warmup score; eviction when node memory/GPUs above 70% usage.

Admission and budgeting

- Admission Controller maintains sliding window counters per tenant (tokens charged for prefetched KV or warm slot). It exposes these signals to billing reconciler but does not alter invoicing in initial rollout — advisory mode.
- Default per-tenant soft budget: 20,000 token-equiv per 24h for small/free tenants; configurable via Console.

Safety and risk mitigations

- Cost guardrails: global cost cap that will disable SPO globally when prefetch token spend rate exceeds threshold for three consecutive minutes.
- Privacy: no persisted customer data is sent to Prefetch Predictor other than hashed prefix ids and aggregated sequence-length histograms.
- Security: all inter-service calls must use mTLS and current service identity tokens.

Operational runbooks (summary)

1. Detection: alert when prefetch.hit rate < 10% while prefetch.approved > 1000/min or when cost.delta token-equiv p95 > 7% for > 30m.
2. Canary rollback: set SPO_ENABLED=false flag via remote feature flag to rapidly disable prefetch for a region.
3. Escalation path: serve-team -> runtime-sre -> infra-oncall.

Rollout plan

- Phase 0 (lab): offline simulation using historical traces, run cost/latency model to tune predictor thresholds. Duration: 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable SPO for 1% of production traffic across 2 regions; monitor p95, cost.delta, and admission drops. Duration: 2-3 weeks.
- Phase 2 (pilot): expand to 10% of traffic and invite 5 enterprise customers to opt-in with detailed dashboards; enable variant-warm for premium customers only.
- Phase 3 (gradual): expand to all traffic with opt-out defaults for small tenants and console controls for per-tenant budgets. Target completion: +3 months after successful pilot.

Success criteria (launch)

- Measured p95 generation latency improvement >= 20% for interactive routes where predictor hit rate >= 25%.
- Token-cost delta p95 < 5% for 95% of tenants.
- No sustained increase in error rate attributable to SPO (errors increase < 0.1% absolute).

Open questions

- Should billing immediately reflect prefetch token-equivalent consumption or stay advisory until 1 quarter after rollout? (Action: Product & Finance decision)
- Predictor model ownership: in-house rules-based vs. lightweight ML — time to production trade-offs.
- Should we provide explicit API for tenants to set tighter budgets programmatically?
